sections.title: Headline
sections.content: Monday’s arXiv biology/biomedicine announcement batch contains ten selected papers spanning clone-aware single-cell analysis, pediatric tumor splicing, protein design, and biomedical signal processing. Today’s agenda: what the papers measure, how far their evidence goes, and which validations remain. arXiv has no official trending chart; this is a relevance-ranked snapshot, not a measured popularity list. Biomedical preprints on arXiv are incomplete coverage of biology and medicine, and this is not a review of bioRxiv, medRxiv, or clinical evidence as a whole.

sections.title: Shared clones make random cell halves look reproducible in pooled screens
sections.abstract: The paper argues that shared descendants of transduced cells can make random halves of pooled single-cell screens appear reproducible, even for null perturbations, and that clone-separated or independently transduced replicates reduce this artifact.
sections.claimed_contribution: The author reports near-universal null agreement under random halves in a primary T-cell screen, versus chance-level agreement between independent replicates, and finds that more cells do not remove the shared-clone component.
sections.unique_caveat: The size estimates vary by screen and cell type; many source screens lack clone labels, and some downstream model comparisons cover only a limited set of states and donors.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Primary q-bio.QM; clone-aware splits and comparisons across 16 screens; public code and results. Semantic Scholar total citations: 0 at snapshot.

sections.title: TAPESTRY: an interactive resource for exploring tumor-enriched splice junctions in pediatric brain tumors
sections.abstract: TAPESTRY is a searchable catalog of recurrent tumor-enriched splice junctions across pediatric brain-tumor histologies, with normal-brain comparisons and annotations intended to help prioritize candidate targets.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors provide filters, expression views, downloadable data, and an API to support prioritization of tumor-enriched and oncofetal splice events. The resource catalogs 45,430 junctions across 19 histologies and 1,962 RNA-seq specimens.
sections.unique_caveat: Junction evidence does not establish stable protein production or HLA presentation. The paper notes limited pediatric normal reference cohorts and heuristic enrichment cutoffs; experimental validation remains necessary.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Primary q-bio.GN; 45,430 junctions, 19 histologies, and 1,962 RNA-seq specimens. Semantic Scholar total citations: 0 at snapshot.

sections.title: Computational De Novo Design of Miniprotein Candidate Neutralizers Targeting the IL-23 Cytokine Subunit p19
sections.abstract: The authors computationally design short protein candidates intended to occupy the IL-23 p19 receptor-binding surface and compare design pipelines using interface-focused structural scores.
sections.claimed_contribution: Their computational comparison finds no reliable predicted interface in the conventional set of 972 designs, while 42 of 50 BindCraft designs exceed the paper’s ipSAE 0.60 threshold.
sections.unique_caveat: These are predictions, not measured binders or neutralizers. The paper reports no affinity assay and uses one partly modeled p19 structure; its score bands are not calibrated for de novo binders.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Primary q-bio.BM; 972 conventional and 50 interface-optimized designs; arXiv comment reports acceptance as a short paper at IEEE BIBM 2026. Semantic Scholar total citations: 0 at snapshot.

sections.title: U-NeXt: General-purpose event detection for neonatal EEG
sections.abstract: U-NeXt applies a shared semantic-segmentation architecture to neonatal EEG event detection, including seizures, artifacts, and low-voltage intervals.
sections.claimed_contribution: The paper reports three development datasets totaling more than 11,000 EEG hours and two independent held-out seizure datasets comprising 130 neonates; U-NeXt+ reached MCC 0.862 and 0.891 on the held-out datasets.
sections.unique_caveat: This is retrospective model evaluation, not evidence of improved outcomes or prospective clinical utility; performance in other hospitals and workflows remains unestablished.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Cross-listed in physics.med-ph; three development datasets and two independent held-out seizure datasets comprising 130 neonates. Semantic Scholar total citations: 0 at snapshot.

sections.title: A Multiscale Kinetic Model of DNA Damage Signalling and Repair under Combined Proton and Nanoparticle Exposure
sections.abstract: This revised model links proton and gold-nanoparticle exposure to double-strand-break induction, DNA-damage signaling, and several modeled repair pathways in human fibroblasts.
sections.claimed_contribution: The author’s model identifies the starting fraction and slower resolution of complex lesions as key drivers of persistent modeled damage under high-LET, nanoparticle-enhanced exposure.
sections.unique_caveat: This is a kinetic model, not a new irradiation experiment. The author flags inconsistent repair-fidelity endpoints and says repair-fate predictions need independent measurements.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Substantive v2 revision in the current q-bio replacement listing; directly links radiation physics to DNA repair mechanisms. Semantic Scholar total citations: 0 at snapshot.

sections.title: Kinetic Proofreading Activation Times Beyond the Weibull Limit
sections.abstract: The authors derive a first-passage description of T-cell receptor activation that retains ligand dissociation and delineates when the commonly used Weibull approximation breaks down.
sections.claimed_contribution: They introduce a dimensionless condition for the Weibull approximation and a closed-form alternative; the approximation matched exact medians within 2 percent in 19 of 25 tested parameter sets.
sections.unique_caveat: Evidence is mathematical and simulation-based; the tested parameter grid does not establish quantitative accuracy in living immune systems.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Primary q-bio.QM; exact continuous-time Markov-chain result plus stochastic simulations. Semantic Scholar total citations: 0 at snapshot.

sections.title: Video-rate quantitative phase and polarimetric imaging (QP2I) for label-free imaging of contracting muscle cells
sections.abstract: QP2I combines single-shot quantitative phase and polarization measurements on a standard DIC microscope to image structural and anisotropic changes in contracting muscle cells.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report video-rate, label-free phase and retardance readouts, including sarcomere length and retardance changes during cardiomyocyte contraction.
sections.unique_caveat: This is an imaging-method validation, not evidence of diagnostic performance or physiological intervention benefit; the abstract does not specify cohort-scale or clinical validation.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Cross-listed in q-bio.QM; tests include simulations, reference targets, fixed tissue, and living moving cells. Semantic Scholar total citations: 0 at snapshot.

sections.title: OPTARI: An open-source software framework for clinical translation of optoacoustic imaging
sections.abstract: OPTARI is a graphical application for processing and analyzing optoacoustic-ultrasound studies, with reconstruction, annotation, segmentation, and temporal/spectral analysis tools.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors describe a vendor-format-aware GUI and report tissue segmentation comparable to expert labeling, with batch processing reduced from minutes to under one second per scan.
sections.unique_caveat: Ongoing clinical studies are not outcome evidence. The abstract does not provide cohort sizes or establish generalization across vendors, tissues, or acquisition protocols.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Cross-listed in physics.med-ph; open-source code; comparison with expert muscle-tissue labels and reported sub-second batch processing. Semantic Scholar total citations: 0 at snapshot.

sections.title: Multilevel Stochastic Plug-and-Play for Sparse-View CT Reconstruction
sections.abstract: The revised method accelerates stochastic plug-and-play CT reconstruction through wavelet multiresolution initialization and coarse-to-fine correction steps.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report reconstruction quality comparable to evaluated stochastic plug-and-play baselines with generally lower runtime, and give convergence conditions for the fine-level iterations.
sections.unique_caveat: The abstract does not establish clinical image quality, patient outcomes, or radiation-dose benefit; it describes two-dataset reconstruction experiments.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: v3 revision in the current physics.med-ph replacement list; two CT datasets and 20–50 projection views. Semantic Scholar total citations: 0 at snapshot.

sections.title: Probe Before You Edit: Probing-Guided Molecular Optimization for LLM Agents in Structure-Based Drug Design
sections.abstract: PROBE uses controlled ligand edits to estimate pocket-specific responses before an LLM-agent optimization loop chooses later molecular changes.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report that PROBE’s site map and edit-response manual improve benchmark performance on CrossDocked2020 and address tradeoffs between binding-score and drug-likeness objectives.
sections.unique_caveat: The evaluation is benchmark/docking-based; it does not establish biochemical binding, developability, or in-vivo efficacy.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: v3 replacement cross-listed in q-bio.BM; arXiv comment reports acceptance at NeurIPS 2026. Semantic Scholar total citations: 1 and influential citations: 0 at snapshot; this is not a batch gain.

sections.title: Trending Research Themes
sections.content: This small batch shows three recurring clusters, not evidence of a field-wide shift: computational models and design with experimental validation gaps; biomedical sensing and reconstruction across EEG, muscle imaging, optoacoustic imaging, and CT; and data context as essential for interpreting single-cell perturbation screens and tumor splice junctions.

sections.title: Open Problems and Research Directions
sections.content: Priorities supported by this corpus include wet-lab expression, affinity, STAT3 blockade, and structural tests for IL-23 binders; independent lesion-class and repair-fidelity measurements for the DNA-damage model; separate transductions and clone barcodes across more Perturb-seq cell types; RNA, protein, and immunopeptidome validation plus broader normal references for TAPESTRY candidates; and prospective multi-site or multi-vendor evaluation of EEG and imaging tools. These are research proposals, not claims of clinical readiness.

sections.title: Takeaway
sections.content: The clearest signal is methodological: trustworthy validation depends on the right experimental unit and adequate biological context. Computational designs and imaging pipelines report promising benchmarks, but independent replication, experimental confirmation, and validation beyond development datasets remain the key gaps.
